provenance: Computed by the LunarWindow pipeline from NASA LOLA terrain and NASA SPICE (DE421) ephemerides. Code written with AI assistance (Claude Code) and verified by the team with automated tests and a comparison against NASA PGDA illumination maps.
verdict: Touchdown 2029-10-13T08 UTC: the Sun's centre is 0.38 deg above the skyline and the top of Earth's disc 0.01 deg above the skyline (power and a link at landing).
Over 14 days: Sun up 100%, Earth in view 100%, both 100% of the time.
Survives the mission: the battery never drops below 140 Wh (lowest 700 Wh).
No darkness during the mission: no cold soak.
Battery needed: 0 Wh of the 560 Wh it can use above its 140 Wh floor.
Battery model: power = panel power x visible Sun, whatever the Sun's direction (a sun-tracking array), so survival is an upper bound for fixed panels.
why: Marginal touchdown: the Sun's centre and the top of Earth's disc clears the skyline by under 0.5 deg; the Sun is 0.38 deg above the skyline (bearing 255 deg, set by terrain 390 m away at 0.93 deg), so there is almost no margin for a landing error, a lower antenna or a later hour.
The Sun stays up all mission: its closest pass, 2029-10-16T10 UTC, is 0.08 deg above the skyline (bearing 218 deg, set by terrain 4.9 km away at 1.00 deg).
Earth stays in view all mission: its closest pass, 2029-10-13T08 UTC, is 0.01 deg above the skyline (bearing 151 deg, set by the Moon's own curvature at -0.75 deg).
